records.issue_text: Dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated at import time so every instance shares the process-start timestamp; should use field(default_factory=timezone.now)
records.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` (a function call). This is executed when the class is defined (module import time), so all `AssignmentSource` instances will get the same `queued` timestamp for the lifetime of the process. This should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to compute a fresh timestamp per instance.
records.stripped_text: Dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated at import time so every instance shares the process-start timestamp; should use field(default_factory=timezone.now)

records.issue_text: Malformed assignment_source_dict silently downgrades to None (sync everything) instead of failing safe; no logging on parse failure in sync_assignee_outbound task
records.rationale: In `sync_assignee_outbound`, malformed `assignment_source_dict` is parsed via `AssignmentSource.from_dict(...)` which returns `None` on `ValueError`/`TypeError` (new `from_dict` in `assignment_source.py`). The task then calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`. Since the cycle-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only triggers when `sync_source` is truthy (`if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == ...: return False`), a parse failure silently becomes `None` and bypasses the new anti-cycle guard, reverting to syncing based solely
